subject.title: AI safety taxonomy: plugin-emitted detectors and evals

question: Should external plugins be allowed to emit AI-safety events into OpenClaw's authoritative diagnostics stream, and if so, what declaration, provenance, privacy, and versioning guarantees must core enforce?
rationale: This creates a permanent public Plugin SDK and manifest contract across a security-sensitive telemetry boundary; code inspection cannot determine the acceptable authority and trust policy without maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve a bounded core contract
options.body: Permit declared event types only after the prerequisite schema is approved, with core validation, immutable untrusted provenance, privacy limits, rejection diagnostics, and compatibility coverage.

options.title: Keep authoritative events core-only
options.body: Allow plugins to run detectors but require them to publish through plugin-owned logs or exporters rather than the core safety-event stream.

options.title: Pause the taxonomy series
options.body: Defer the plugin API and linked PR until the umbrella observability direction has explicit sponsorship and an agreed end-to-end design.

recommendation.title: Approve a bounded core contract
recommendation.body: Permit declared event types only after the prerequisite schema is approved, with core validation, immutable untrusted provenance, privacy limits, rejection diagnostics, and compatibility coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision combines product direction with the diagnostics architecture introduced in steipete's earlier work.
